verification.reason: The mechanism is real. In `misses()` the filter keeps only reports whose own reason is in `--reason`, then takes the first. If a group's first report is `owned-missed` and its second is `needs-execution`, `--reason needs-execution` exports the second. `stats()` at lines 803-807 files the same group under the first in-scope reason, `owned-missed`. So one defect can reach both corpora, and `needs-execution` can export a group that stats counts as `owned-missed`. But the selection rule is deliberate and documented. The doc comment on `misses()` says "A report with another reason ... is passed over". `docs/guidelines/cli.md:29` says the export takes "the first report of its group in site order that a person judged valid with a reason `--reason` names". The tests at comparison.test.ts:1828-1833 pin per-reason filtering. The base clause "Each defect contributes one miss" is about stats. A single export, with all reasons or with one, still writes at most one miss per defect. Whether the same defect may appear in two separately filtered exports when a maintainer has judged the reports in one group differently is a design question. The code does not clearly break the base decision, so I cannot confirm it. Two mismatched per-report reasons in one group are needed, so the case is also narrow.
